questions.question: The first and last terms of an A.P. are 28 and 31. If the sum of its terms is 236, then the number of terms will be?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Number of terms (n) = (2 × Sum) ÷ (First term + Last term)

n = (2 × 236) ÷ (28 + 31)

n = 472 ÷ 59

n = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 28

Last term (l) = 31

Sum of terms (Sₙ) = 236

**Formula Used:**

Sₙ = (n/2) × (a + l)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df204b1d9caa7e4add7647aff0cbb77418e453a122a7b8fc58a440dcc4e7accd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 236 = (n/2) × (28 + 31)

⇒ 236 = (n/2) × 59

⇒ 236 × 2 = 59n

⇒ 472 = 59n

⇒ n = 472 ÷ 59

⇒ n = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression General Term

The nth term of an A.P. is given by aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where d is the common difference.

Sum of n terms (General formula)

Sₙ = (n/2) × [2a + (n − 1)d], used when the common difference is known.

Common Difference formula

d = (Last term − First term) ÷ (n − 1).</p

questions.question: A and B are two independent events. If P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.6, then the P(A or B) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__**Calculation:**__

 

Given,

Probability of event **A**, P(A) = 0.4

Probability of event **B**, P(B) = 0.6

For **independent events** A and B,

P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)

⇒ P(A ∩ B) = 0.4 × 0.6 = 0.24

According to the **addition theorem** of probability,

P(A or B) = P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

⇒ P(A ∪ B) = 0.4 + 0.6 − 0.24

⇒ P(A ∪ B) = 1.0 − 0.24

⇒ P(A ∪ B) = 0.76

**∴ The value of P(A or B) is 0.76.**

questions.question: The minimum value of 8x + 14 + 3x² is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
For a **quadratic expression** ax² + bx + c where a > 0, the **minimum value** occurs at x = −b / 2a.

Given: 3x² + 8x + 14 (a = 3, b = 8, c = 14).

Min Value = (4ac − b²) / 4a = (4 × 3 × 14 − 8²) / (4 × 3).

Min Value = (168 − 64) / 12 = 104 / 12 = 26 / 3 = 8(2/3).

**∴ The correct answer is 8(2/3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expression 3x² + 8x + 14.

**Formula Used:** To find the **extrema** of f(x), set the first derivative f'(x) = 0.

⇒ Let f(x) = 3x² + 8x + 14

⇒ f'(x) = d/dx(3x² + 8x + 14) = 6x + 8

⇒ Set f'(x) = 0 ⇒ 6x + 8 = 0 ⇒ x = −8/6 = −4/3

⇒ f''(x) = 6 (Since f''(x) > 0, it is a **minimum**)

⇒ Minimum value = 3(−4/3)² + 8(−4/3) + 14

⇒ Min value = 3(16/9) − 32/3 + 14

⇒ Min value = 16/3 − 32/3 + 14 = −16/3 + 14

⇒ Min value = (−16 + 42) / 3 = 26/3 = 8(2/3)

**∴ The correct answer is 8(2/3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quadratic Extrema

For ax² + bx + c, if **a > 0**, the parabola opens upwards and has a **minimum**. If **a < 0**, it has a **maximum**.

Vertex Formula

The coordinates of the vertex (h, k) are given by h = −b/2a and k = c − b²/4a.

Discriminant Relationship

The discriminant D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of roots, while the vertex value is −D/4a.</p

questions.question: If the quadratic equation x² − 4ax + (b + 1) = 0, where a and b are real constants, has no real roots, then:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0 to have **no real roots**, the **Discriminant (D)** must be less than zero (D (2a + 1)(2a − 1)

**∴ The correct answer is b > (2a + 1)(2a − 1).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x² − 4ax + (b + 1) = 0

**Formula Used:** For no real roots, **Discriminant (D) = B² − 4AC (2a)² − 1²

⇒ b > (2a + 1)(2a − 1)

**∴ The correct answer is b > (2a + 1)(2a − 1).**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The value D = b² − 4ac determines the nature: D > 0 (real and distinct), D = 0 (real and equal), and D < 0 (no real roots/imaginary).

Difference of Squares

The identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is frequently used to factorize quadratic expressions in inequalities.</p

questions.question: If three cards are drawn one by one randomly from a pack of 52 cards, then what is the probability that three of them are jack?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Jacks** in a deck = 4. Total cards = 52.

Probability for 1st Jack = 4/52. Probability for 2nd Jack = 3/51. Probability for 3rd Jack = 2/50.

Required Probability = (4 × 3 × 2) ÷ (52 × 51 × 50)

Simplified Result = 1 ÷ (13 × 17 × 25) = 1/5525.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0433a1eafcacefd5939df80b85ec229ccb2ea47799b3ffef3d3bea9af734f9b.png] 

**Given:** Total cards = 52, Number of Jacks = 4.

**Formula:** Probability P(E) = n(E) ÷ n(S) or ⁿCᵣ method.

⇒ Total ways to draw 3 cards = ⁵²C₃

⇒ Favorable ways to draw 3 Jacks = ⁴C₃

⇒ Required Probability = ⁴C₃ ÷ ⁵²C₃

⇒ Required Probability = 4 ÷ [(52 × 51 × 50) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1)]

⇒ Required Probability = (4 × 6) ÷ (52 × 51 × 50)

⇒ Required Probability = 24 ÷ 132600

⇒ Required Probability = 1/5525

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combinations Formula

The number of ways to select r items from n is ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r! × (n−r)!].

Deck Composition

A standard deck has 52 cards: 4 suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) with 13 cards each, including 4 **Face Cards** of each type (King, Queen, Jack).

Multiplication Rule

For dependent events (without replacement), P(A and B and C) = P(A) × P(B|A) × P(C|A and B).</p

questions.question: The point (9, 0), (9, 6), (-9, 6) and (-9, 0) are the vertices of a _________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **coordinates**: A(9, 0), B(9, 6), C(−9, 6), and D(−9, 0).

The **width** (horizontal distance) is constant for pairs: |9 − (−9)| = 18 units.

The **height** (vertical distance) is constant for pairs: |6 − 0| = 6 units.

Since **opposite sides are equal** (18 and 6) and **adjacent sides are unequal** with **right angles** (axes are perpendicular), it is a **rectangle**.

**∴ The correct answer is rectangle.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Vertices A(9, 0), B(9, 6), C(−9, 6), D(−9, 0).

**Formula Used:** Distance = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f2eca96f97e1f29c01f0cdc967347c7df76054fd1ea865e47998451ea48adae.png] 

⇒ Side AB = √((9 − 9)² + (6 − 0)²) = √(0 + 36) = 6 units

⇒ Side BC = √((−9 − 9)² + (6 − 6)²) = √((−18)² + 0) = 18 units

⇒ Side CD = √((−9 − (−9))² + (0 − 6)²) = √(0 + 36) = 6 units

⇒ Side DA = √((9 − (−9))² + (0 − 0)²) = √(18² + 0) = 18 units

⇒ Since **opposite sides are equal** (AB = CD and BC = DA) and **adjacent sides are perpendicular**, the figure is a **rectangle**.

**∴ The correct answer is rectangle.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rectangle

Opposite sides are **equal and parallel**, and all interior angles are **90 degrees**.

Distance Formula

The distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).

Quadrilateral Identification

If all sides are equal and angles are 90°, it is a **square**; if only opposite sides are equal and angles are 90°, it is a **rectangle**.

questions.question: In a survey of 260 students in a school, 100 were listed as taking apple juice, 150 as taking orange juice and 75 were listed as taking both apple as well as orange juice. Find how many students were taking neither apple juice nor orange juice.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total students (n(U)) = 260

At least one juice = n(Apple) + n(Orange) − n(Both) = 100 + 150 − 75 = 175

Neither juice = Total students − At least one juice = 260 − 175 = 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students surveyed = 260

Students taking **Apple juice** (n(A)) = 100

Students taking **Orange juice** (n(O)) = 150

Students taking **Both juices** (n(A ∩ O)) = 75

**Formula Used:**

n(A ∪ O) = n(A) + n(O) − n(A ∩ O)

Students taking neither = Total − n(A ∪ O)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42cbb40842faa8181b348ec211591d5b0ad6968e9e9fa5f4c1c9ab57dc5210d6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Students taking at least one juice = 100 + 150 − 75

⇒ n(A ∪ O) = 175

⇒ Students taking neither juice = 260 − 175

⇒ Result = 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Venn Diagram Basics

A Venn diagram represents sets as circles within a rectangle (Universal set). The overlap represents the intersection (A ∩ B).

De Morgan's Laws

The number of elements in neither set is denoted by (A ∪ B)' which is equal to n(U) − n(A ∪ B).

Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion

For three sets: n(A∪B∪C) = n(A)+n(B)+n(C) − n(A∩B) − n(B∩C) − n(C∩A) + n(A∩B∩C).</p

questions.question: The mode and median of a data is 87.5 and 86, respectively. What is the mean of the data? (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Substitute **Mode** = 87.5 and **Median** = 86.

87.5 = 3 × 86 − 2 × Mean

2 × Mean = 258 − 87.5 = 170.5

Mean = 170.5 ÷ 2 = 85.25 ≈ 85.2.

**∴ The correct answer is 85.2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mode** = 87.5

**Median** = 86

**Formula Used:**

**Empirical Relationship:** (**Mean** − **Mode**) = 3 × (**Mean** − **Median**)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Mean** be 'x'.

⇒ x − 87.5 = 3 × (x − 86)

⇒ x − 87.5 = 3x − 258

⇒ 3x − x = 258 − 87.5

⇒ 2x = 170.5

⇒ x = 170.5 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 85.25

**∴ The correct answer is 85.2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

Used for **moderately skewed distributions**: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Skewness Identification

If **Mean > Median > Mode**, the distribution is **positively skewed**. If **Mode > Median > Mean**, it is **negatively skewed**.</p

questions.question: Two dice (both numbered 1 to 6) are rolled, simultaneously. What is the probability of observing a sum of 8?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Total outcomes when two dice are rolled = 6² = 36.

For a sum of **n** where 2 ≤ n ≤ 7, the number of outcomes is (n − 1).

For a sum of **n** where 8 ≤ n ≤ 12, the number of outcomes is (13 − n).

Favorable outcomes for **sum 8** = 13 − 8 = 5.

Probability = 5 ÷ 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/36.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72349c1954fb1b3aea664ee9d0e94227a762a8080439628fc4b992e92c890691.png] 
**Given:** Two dice are rolled simultaneously.

**Formula:** Probability P(E) = (Number of favorable outcomes) ÷ (Total number of possible outcomes)

⇒ Total outcomes n(S) = 6 × 6 = 36

⇒ Possible pairs for **Sum = 8**: (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2)

⇒ Number of favorable outcomes n(E) = 5

⇒ P(E) = 5/36

**∴ The correct answer is 5/36.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sample Space of Dice

When **n** dice are rolled, the total number of outcomes is 6ⁿ.

Sum Range

For two dice, the **minimum sum** is 2 (1+1) and the **maximum sum** is 12 (6+6).

Most Frequent Sum

The sum **7** has the highest probability (6/36 = 1/6) as it has the most combinations (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1).</p

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle measures 132°. What is the measure of each of the base angles?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle**, the **base angles** are equal.

Sum of all angles in a triangle = 180°

Base Angle = (180° − **Vertex Angle**) ÷ 2

Base Angle = (180° − 132°) ÷ 2 = 48° ÷ 2 = 24°.

**∴ The correct answer is 24° and 24°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Vertex Angle** (A) = 132°

Triangle type = **Isosceles Triangle**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be71913fba9e9486dc4f4abee91249ad8a7bde25ad4d964a88101178b566b7ce.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

For isosceles ΔABC, if AB = AC, then ∠B = ∠C.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the equal **base angles** be x° each.

⇒ 132° + x° + x° = 180°

⇒ 132° + 2x° = 180°

⇒ 2x° = 180° − 132°

⇒ 2x° = 48°

⇒ x° = 24°

**∴ The correct answer is 24° and 24°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Triangle Property

In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite to the equal sides are always equal.

Equilateral Triangle

A special case where all three sides and all three angles are equal (each angle is 60°).

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the interior angles of any triangle on a Euclidean plane is always 180°.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the lengths of two corresponding sides of two similar triangles is 6 : 2. The ratio of the areas of these two triangles, in the order mentioned, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is the **square** of the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Ratio of sides = 6 : 2

Ratio of areas = 6² : 2² = 36 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 36 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of corresponding sides (s₁ : s₂) = 6 : 2

**Formula Used:**

If two triangles are **similar**, then Area₁ / Area₂ = (side₁ / side₂)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c42b25d52313302c7b9d45ccf4c50692835233770647d04a7012577cca1bc818.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the area of the first triangle be A₁ and the second be A₂.

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = (6 / 2)²

⇒ A₁ / A₂ = 36 / 4

⇒ Ratio of areas = 36 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 36 : 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area Ratio Property

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding altitudes, medians, or angle bisector segments.

Perimeter Ratio Property

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides (Linear Ratio).</p

questions.question: The value of the discriminant of the quadratic equation 7x² - 18x - 11 = 0 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify coefficients: **a = 7**, **b = −18**, **c = −11**.

Use the **Discriminant** formula: **D = b² − 4ac**.

D = (−18)² − 4 × 7 × (−11) = 324 + 308 = 632.

**∴ The correct answer is 632.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Quadratic Equation **7x² − 18x − 11 = 0**

**Formula Used:** For a general quadratic equation **ax² + bx + c = 0**, the **Discriminant (D)** is given by: **D = b² − 4ac**

⇒ Comparing **7x² − 18x − 11 = 0** with **ax² + bx + c = 0**

⇒ **a = 7**

⇒ **b = −18**

⇒ **c = −11**

⇒ **D = (−18)² − 4 × 7 × (−11)**

⇒ **D = 324 − (−308)**

⇒ **D = 324 + 308**

⇒ **D = 632**

**∴ The correct answer is 632.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

If **D > 0**, the roots are **real and distinct**. If **D = 0**, the roots are **real and equal**. If **D < 0**, the roots are **imaginary**.

Quadratic Formula

The roots of the equation are calculated as **x = (−b ± √D) ÷ 2a**.

Sum and Product of Roots

Sum of roots = **−b/a** and Product of roots = **c/a**.</p

questions.question: The coordinates of a point A, where AB is the diameter of a circle whose centre is (2, – 3) and B is (1, 4) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the property that **Centre** is the **Midpoint** of the **Diameter**.

Let **A** = (x, y). Then Midpoint = ((x+1)÷2, (y+4)÷2) = (2, −3).

Equating x-coordinates: x + 1 = 4 ⇒ x = 3.

Equating y-coordinates: y + 4 = −6 ⇒ y = −10.

**∴ The correct answer is (3, −10).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Centre **O** = (2, −3) and point **B** = (1, 4). **AB** is the **diameter**.

**Formula Used:** Midpoint Formula: M = ((x₁ + x₂)÷2, (y₁ + y₂)÷2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44175fa6bc8dbf42cc81c42ffd68f2adc826503076dbc2de4ac39b70fceacc97.png] 

⇒ Let coordinates of point **A** be (x, y).

⇒ Since **AB** is the diameter, **Centre O** is the midpoint of **AB**.

⇒ (x + 1) ÷ 2 = 2

⇒ x + 1 = 4 ⇒ x = 3

⇒ (y + 4) ÷ 2 = −3

⇒ y + 4 = −6 ⇒ y = −10

**∴ The correct answer is (3, −10).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Midpoint Formula

The midpoint of a segment with endpoints (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by ((x₁+x₂)÷2, (y₁+y₂)÷2).

Diameter Property

A diameter of a circle is the longest chord and its midpoint is always the centre of the circle.

Section Formula

The midpoint formula is a special case of the section formula where the ratio m:n is 1:1.</p

questions.question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 10 and 360, respectively. If one of the numbers is (4)/(9) times of the other, what is the smaller numbher?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Product of two numbers = **HCF × LCM**

Let the numbers be **9x** and **4x** based on the ratio 4 : 9.

9x × 4x = 10 × 360 ⇒ 36x² = 3600 ⇒ x² = 100 ⇒ x = 10.

Smaller number = 4x = 4 × 10 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** HCF = 10, LCM = 360. Ratio of numbers = 4/9 : 1 ⇒ 4 : 9.

**Formula Used:** Product of two numbers = **HCF × LCM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d1b92b19b0514ed02196ae12df431c403fd65894b6e9741c61ead2cf4ad2d36.png] 

⇒ Let the larger number be **y** and the smaller number be (4/9)y.

⇒ y × (4/9)y = 10 × 360

⇒ (4/9)y² = 3600

⇒ y² = (3600 × 9) ÷ 4

⇒ y² = 900 × 9 = 8100

⇒ y = √8100 = 90

⇒ Smaller number = (4/9) × 90 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property of HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b, **LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b**.

HCF as a Factor

The **HCF** of two or more numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**.

Ratio and HCF

If the ratio of two numbers is a : b and their HCF is H, then the numbers are **Ha** and **Hb**, and their LCM is **Hab**.</p

questions.question: If the height of a tower is √3 times its shadow, then the angle of the elevation of the top of the tower is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between **Height** (H) and **Shadow** (S) is given as H = √3 × S.

In a right-angled triangle, **tan θ** = Height ÷ Shadow.

⇒ tan θ = (√3 × S) ÷ S = √3.

Since tan 60° = √3, the **Angle of Elevation** is 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of the tower (h) = √3 × length of shadow (s).

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19ae3629dc4c1f81d2185f6d20d8e3c5cfbfe1075f708fd694de45a3573205a1.png] 

Let the length of the **Shadow** (BC) be x units.

⇒ **Height** of the tower (AB) = √3x units.

In right ΔABC, let the **Angle of Elevation** ∠ACB = θ.

⇒ tan θ = AB ÷ BC

⇒ tan θ = √3x ÷ x

⇒ tan θ = √3

⇒ tan θ = tan 60°

⇒ θ = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

Common values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, and tan 90° is undefined.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The **Angle of Elevation** is the angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight when looking up at an object.

Height and Shadow Property

When the angle of elevation is 45°, the height of the object is exactly equal to the length of its shadow.</p

questions.question: Let C₁ and C₂ be two circles which do not externally touch and intersect each other and O₁ , and O₂ be the centers of the circles, respectively. Let AB be the common transverse tangent to the circles such that P, Q are the points of tangency respectively to C₁ , C₂ . Let R be the point of intersection of O₁ O₂ and AB. If ∠PO₁R = 60°, find ∠QO₂R and ∠QRO₂ , respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **transverse common tangent** configuration, the triangles formed by the centers, points of tangency, and the intersection point on the center line are **similar triangles**.

⇒ ΔO₁PR ∼ ΔO₂QR because both are right-angled at the tangency points and share vertically opposite angles at R.

⇒ ∠QO₂R = ∠PO₁R = 60°.

⇒ In ΔO₂QR, ∠QRO₂ = 180° − (90° + 60°) = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60° and 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Centers **O₁** and **O₂**, Transverse tangent **PQ**, Intersection point **R** on O₁O₂, and ∠PO₁R = 60°.

**Formula:** Radius is always **perpendicular** to the tangent at the point of contact (∠O₁PR = ∠O₂QR = 90°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07d390f669e709b809b7ac7d45e813948db538eb745ea957c84d364c74fcde21.png] 

⇒ In ΔO₁PR, ∠O₁PR = 90° and ∠PO₁R = 60°.

⇒ Sum of angles in triangle = 180° → ∠PRO₁ = 180° − (90° + 60°) = 30°.

⇒ ∠QRO₂ = ∠PRO₁ = 30° (**Vertically opposite angles**).

⇒ In ΔO₂QR, ∠O₂QR = 90° (**Radius ⊥ Tangent**).

⇒ ∠QO₂R = 180° − (∠O₂QR + ∠QRO₂) = 180° − (90° + 30°) = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60° and 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Transverse Common Tangent Length

The length of the TCT is given by √(d² − (R + r)²), where d is the distance between centers.

Internal Division by Intersection Point

The point R divides the line segment O₁O₂ internally in the ratio of the radii R₁ : R₂.

Tangent Property

A line is tangent to a circle if and only if it is perpendicular to the radius at the point of intersection.</p

questions.question: A coin is thrown eight times. The probability of getting exactly five tails is:
questions.solution:
__**Calculation:**__

 

Given,

Number of trials, n = 8

Probability of getting a **tail**, p = 1/2

Probability of not getting a **tail**, q = 1/2

Required number of successes, r = 5

The **Binomial Distribution** formula is,

\(P(X = r) = ^{n}C_{r} \cdot p^
